title: Payroll Assistant
description:
Overview:
Zenith Advisory Partners are working with a reputable and established business in Carlisle that are seeking an organised, accurate and proactive Payroll Assistant to join a busy payroll team within a leading business.
This is an excellent opportunity for someone with payroll experience who enjoys working in a fast-paced environment and wants to develop their career within payroll. You will play a key role in ensuring their employees are paid accurately and on time, supporting payroll processing across a diverse workforce.
Key Responsibilities:
- Process, manage and maintain both the monthly payroll and Time and Attendance software accurately and within agreed deadlines.
- Maintain accurate employee payroll records, including starters, leavers and amendments.
- Process overtime, allowances, deductions, and other payroll adjustments.
- Manage payroll queries from employees and managers, providing professional and timely responses.
- Complete statutory payroll requirements, including PAYE, National Insurance, pensions and statutory payments.
- Ensure all payroll changes are supported by appropriate authorisation.
- Reconcile payroll reports and investigate discrepancies.
- Liaise with HR, Finance and operational teams to resolve payroll issues.
- Support year-end processes, including P60s and other statutory reporting.
- Assist with payroll audits and continuous improvement initiatives.

Skills & Experience Required:
- Experienced in payroll administration, ideally within a high-volume payroll environment.
- Highly organised with excellent attention to detail.
- Confident working with numbers and identifying discrepancies.
- Comfortable working to tight deadlines.
- Able to handle confidential and sensitive information appropriately.
- A strong communicator with excellent customer service skills.
- Competent using Microsoft Excel and payroll systems.
- Able to work independently while also being a strong team player.
- Keen to develop their knowledge and career within payroll.

What's on Offer:
- Salary up to £30,000, depending on experience.
- 33 days of annual leave (including bank holidays)
- Company pension - 5%
- Sick pay
- Additional leave
- Employee discount
- Health & wellbeing programme
- On-site parking
- Referral programme

title: Administrator
description:
Location: Cumberland Infirmary, Carlisle Salary: Competitive, depending on experience Hours: Monday-Friday, 9:30am-2:00pm (22.5 hours per week) Job Type: Permanent, Part-Time

We are looking for an experienced Consumables Stock Controller to join our client's team at Cumberland Infirmary. This is a great opportunity for someone with a background in stock control, warehousing or inventory management who is organised, accurate and enjoys working in a busy environment.

Key Responsibilities
- Manage stock levels, inventory and ordering of consumables.
- Receive, check, store and rotate stock.
- Carry out regular stock checks and reconciliations.
- Manage stock transfers, recalls, expired products and discrepancies.
- Liaise with suppliers, procurement and finance teams.
- Provide stock support to clinical teams.

Essential
- Minimum 3 years' warehousing/inventory management experience.
- Strong stock control experience.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Excel.
- Excellent organisation and attention to detail.
- Strong communication and administration skills.

Desirable
- Previous NHS or healthcare experience.
- Warehouse management experience.
- Full UK driving licence, as occasional travel may be required.

Please note: An Enhanced DBS check will be required for the successful applicant.

title: Receptionist - Bank
company: Hamberley Care Management Limited - Company - Permanent
description:
Be all you can be with Hamberley
At Hamberley, we believe that our residents deserve something 'Extra Special, Every Day' and we're recruiting for a Receptionist to help us achieve our goals.
Working as our receptionist, you will be responsible for the Reception area of the home, ensuring this is presented to a high standard at all times.
Joining us at Montague House, our luxury care home that provides residential, dementia, and nursing care for older people, you'll be part of a team that is genuinely passionate about the health and well-being of our residents.
We offer our colleagues
- A competitive salary and benefits package
- 28 days holiday inclusive of Bank Holidays
- Quality-linked bonus scheme - A performance bonus tied to our CQC/CI quality rating, rewarding you for helping us deliver outstanding care.
- Workplace pension for your future security
- A true team culture - A collaborative, encouraging working environment where kindness, respect, and professional pride are at the heart of everything we do
- Excellent training and career development opportunities
- Employee Assistance Programme, occupational health and wellbeing support services
- Everyday saving perks - Access to a wide range of retail discounts and savings
- Free on-site parking
- Rewarding connections - Refer a Friend bonus - earn up to £750 per successful referral because great people know great people.

What you'll be doing:
- Greeting and directing visitors, family members, residents, district nurses and contractors to the home and around the home as appropriate.
- Be the first point of contact for visitors and third parties contacting the home, ensuring queries are dealt with and/or directed in a timely manner.
- Answering incoming telephone calls, ensuring calls are documented and/or redirected accordingly.

Could you be part of our team?
About you:
- Possess demonstrable experience working within a Customer Service/Receptionist and/or Administrative environment or similar role.
- Proficient in use of Microsoft Office, particularly Word and Excel.
- A caring, patient, and respectful demeanor.
- Excellent attention to detail and organizational skills.
- Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
- To share our values and demonstrate them at all times. "Can-Do" flexible team worker, problem solver, passion for what they do, ability to manage diverse and demanding workload, think out of the box, open to doing things differently.

If this sounds like you and you're looking for a fulfilling role that makes a genuine impact in the lives of others, this rewarding career is for you.
Due to the high level of interest we anticipate for this role, we may close this advert earlier than the stated closing date to manage applications effectively. If you're interested in joining us at Hamberley, we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.
About Montague House
Montague House is a luxurious care home in Brampton, part of the award-winning Hamberley Care Homes - offering luxury care homes in beautiful locations throughout the UK. Residents live in spacious, stylish ensuite rooms, and enjoy beautifully furnished shared spaces and landscaped gardens. From the deluxe picture house - where we screen classic films - to the on-site luxury spa - offering hairdressing, manicures and relaxing therapies - everything has been designed and finished with the care and attention you would expect from a 5-star hotel.
Hamberley People
We respect and value our residents and each other. At Hamberley Care Homes, we believe in the importance of what we do and why we do it. Creative and empowered, our people see every day as an opportunity for growth and development. We make ideas happen. Together we can achieve anything.
Be part of something special. Be part of Hamberley.

title: Practice Receptionist
location: Carlisle, CA1 3UB, Carlisle, CA1 1DG, CARLISLE, CA3 9JZ
description: We are looking for two friendly, organised, and professional Practice Receptionists to join our busy GP practice team. The successful candidates will be the first point of contact for patients, providing a welcoming and helpful service while supporting the smooth day-to-day running of the practice. We have two part time positions available with the following work patterns and weekly working hours: Position 1 - 27.5 hours per week Monday: 8am to 2pm Tuesday: 10am to 8:30pm Wednesday: 12:30pm to 6:30pm Friday: 8am to 2pm Position 2 - 20.5 hours per week Monday: 8am to 6:30pm Wednesday: 8am to 2pm Saturday: 8:30am to 1:30pm Interviews will be held on the 24th November. To provide a friendly, professional and efficient reception and call handling service, welcoming patients and visitors, managing enquiries and directing patients to the appropriate healthcare service or professional. To support the practice team with daily administrative tasks and ensure the smooth running of the practice whilst maintaining patient confidentiality. Welcoming patients and visitors to the practice in a professional, friendly and courteous manner. Answering phone calls, responding to patient enquiries and directing calls to the appropriate healthcare professional. Booking, cancelling and rearranging appointments through practice patient systems. Registering new and temporary patients and updating patient records, ensuring all information is accurate. Monitor, review, and process incoming eConsult and other online consultation requests through the day. Assist patients who experience difficulties accessing or completing digital consultation forms Where appropriate and in accordance with practice protocols, direct patients to suitable services such as self-care resources, local pharmacies, or NHS 111. Maintain patient confidentiality and handle sensitive information in accordance with GDPR and practice policies. Manage incoming and outgoing correspondence, emails and other administrative documentation. Process repeat prescription requests in line with practice procedures. Liaising with healthcare professionals, including GPs, to support the smooth running of the practice. Respond to patient enquiries with sensitivity and professionalism, identifying urgent matters and referring them to the appropriate healthcare professional as required. Maintaining an organised reception area. Undertake general administrative duties, ensuring patient information and documentation are handled securely. Adhere to practice policies and procedures. Support the day to day running of the practice while working collaboratively with colleagues and healthcare professionals to deliver a high standard of patient care. Where required open and close surgeries in line with practice procedure. Undertake any other reasonable duties appropriate to the roles as requested by the practice manager or partners.
